title: Production Incident: Node.js Container OOMKilled Memory Leak
businessContext: The core API service in the production Kubernetes cluster is crashing every 4 hours with exit code 137 (OOMKilled). Customer checkout requests are intermittently dropped during pod restarts, and P99 latency degrades significantly before each crash.
problemStatement: Investigate the production incident using the provided Prometheus memory metrics, application logs, and recent commit diffs. Formulate the root-cause hypothesis, identify immediate mitigation, implement a permanent fix, define regression tests, and configure monitoring alerts to prevent future occurrences.
constraints: Immediate mitigation must stabilize production within 10 minutes without data loss.
Must identify exact memory retention pattern in application code.
Permanent fix must keep RSS memory flat under 250MB.

candidateTasks: Step 1: State the root-cause hypothesis supported by specific evidence from logs, metrics, and git diff.
Step 2: Propose immediate mitigation to stop the crash loop immediately.
Step 3: Provide permanent code fix (bounded LRU cache or stream buffer with max size and TTL).
Step 4: Write regression test verifying memory usage does not scale linearly with request count.
Step 5: Define Prometheus alerting rule (`container_memory_working_set_bytes > 85% for 5m`).
hints: Look closely at the recent deployment commit `c4e910a`: an unbounded array `requestHistory` in global module scope.
Every HTTP request appends `req.body` and user objects into `requestHistory`, which is never cleaned or pruned.
Immediate mitigation: Roll back to previous commit `c4e910a^` or scale deployment with a temporary increased memory limit.
alternativeApproaches: Sending structured logs to stdout and letting Fluentbit / Vector ship logs to Datadog/Elasticsearch.
commonMistakes: Increasing pod memory limit from 1GB to 4GB: an unbounded leak will simply take 16 hours to crash instead of 4 hours.
Trying to manually run `global.gc()` in production.
